title: Promoting Liberty and Prosperity Amid the COVID-19 Pandemic
primary_topics: Welcome address by CJP as ALA Philippines Chairman at an ALA Philippines/AIM webinar on Philippine Foreign Investment Rules and the ASEAN Comprehensive Investment Agreement, August 24, 2020
Why discuss investments during COVID-19: forward-looking recovery planning and the organized-response principle -- unity produces better results than isolated actions

ALA Philippines' institutional history: founding by late Senator Angara (1979), Manila's first General Assembly (1980), Filipino presidents (Angara, Fernan, Cruz), and the AsnLI inaugural (April 2019)
The liberty-and-prosperity philosophy applied to ASEAN investment: 'integrity and investments' as a specific twin-beacon pairing for the business-law context
sub_topics: ALA's founding and ASEAN recognition: founded 1979 as the premier organization of judges, government lawyers, private practitioners and law professors in Southeast Asia; recognized in ASEAN Charter as ASEAN's lone accredited civil society organization for law

ALA's aim: 'to provide the organizational framework for regional cooperation in the study of, and research in, the laws of the ASEAN countries with a view to harmonizing them as required by the social and economic development of the ASEAN region'

ALA Philippines' role: hosted first General Assembly in Manila 1980; three Filipino ALA presidents: late Senator Edgardo Angara (founding), late CJ Marcelo B. Fernan, and Atty. Ave Cruz (now chairman of the ASEAN Law Institute/AsnLI)

AsnLI creation: Prof. Andre Palacios prepared the concept paper at ALA Philippines' request; ALA Philippines sponsored the creation at ALA Governing Council meetings; ALA Philippines hosted the AsnLI inaugural in April 2019
AIM as co-organizer: Dr. Jikyeong Kang heads AIM; CJP's sentimental connection -- Leni taught at AIM for 39 years, daughter Maria Theresa Manalac (Tet) teaches there now

Two reasons to discuss investments during COVID-19: (1) forward-looking -- once the worst is over, ASEAN needs more investments to boost economies; address public health AND keep an eye on recovery steps; (2) organized response -- the Agreement is the organized response to scarcity from risk and uncertainty; unity produces far better results than isolated, uncoordinated actions
ASEAN as single market and production base: free flow of investments among ASEAN countries; uniform protection, promotion and facilitation across the region

Liberty-and-prosperity formula expanded: 'justice and jobs; freedom and food; ethics and economics; integrity and investments; peace and development; liberty and prosperity; these twin beacons must always go together; one is useless without the other' -- the specific addition of 'integrity and investments' for the business-law audience
ALA General Assembly February 26, 2015 citation: the same address where CJP most fully articulated the philosophy (also referenced in SA015)

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered August 24, 2020 as the welcome address at an ALA Philippines/AIM webinar on Philippine Foreign Investment Rules and the ASEAN Comprehensive Investment Agreement, this short speech by CJP -- as ALA Philippines Chairman -- establishes the institutional context (ALA founded 1979, recognized in the ASEAN Charter as ASEAN's lone accredited civil society law organization, with the Philippines hosting the first General Assembly in 1980 and producing three ALA presidents: the late Senator Angara, the late CJ Fernan, and Atty. Ave Cruz, now chairman of the AsnLI which ALA Philippines pioneered in April 2019) and explains why it makes sense to discuss investment rules during a pandemic: first, being forward-looking -- ASEAN needs investment-promotion infrastructure ready for post-COVID recovery; second, the organized response principle -- 'we are in this together and... an organized response produces far better results than isolated actions.' He notes his sentimental connection to co-organizer AIM through Leni (39 years of teaching) and daughter Tet (now teaching there). He closes by linking the webinar's topic to his signature philosophy, with one domain-specific extension for the business-law audience: 'justice and jobs; freedom and food; ethics and economics; integrity and investments; peace and development; liberty and prosperity -- these twin beacons must always go together; one is useless without the other.'
